LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChainOf: Under the law p, X → Y → Z is a Markov chain when X and Z are conditionally independent given Y.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChain: A joint law of (A,B,C) is Markov in coordinate order when its first and third coordinates are conditionally independent given the second.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_iff: A joint law p of (A,B,C) is Markov in that order exactly when p(a,b,c) pᴮ(b) = pᴬᴮ(a,b) pᴮᶜ(b,c) for every a,b,c, where the superscripts denote marginals. This form also covers b of zero probability.
For finite endpoint alphabets, A → B → C is Markov exactly when the conditional joint law of (A,C) given B = b is a product law for every b with positive probability.
For finite-valued endpoints A and C, A → B → C is Markov exactly when A and C are independent under each conditional law given B = b with Pr(B = b) > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued X, Y and Z with a common source law, I(X;Z | Y) = 0 if and only if X → Y → Z is a Markov chain.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChainOf_r: Let X, Y and Z be functions of a common outcome with probability mass function p. Then Z → Y → X is a Markov chain under p if and only if X → Y → Z is a Markov chain under p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_map: Reversing the coordinate order of a triple preserves the Markov property: (C,B,A) has a Markov law exactly when (A,B,C) does.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSndCh: For a pair (A,B) with finite-valued A, this channel from B to A assigns the conditional law of A given B = b to each b of positive probability. At b of zero probability it returns the marginal law of A as a default.
If Pr(B = b) = 0, the row at b of the library’s total channel from B to finite-valued A is the marginal law of A, by its choice of default.
If Pr(B = b) > 0, the row at b of the total channel from B to finite-valued A is the conditional law of A given B = b.
If Pr(B = b) = 0, multiplying any row probability q(a) by Pr(B = b) gives the same value, zero, as using the total conditional channel’s row at b.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_mul_c: For a pair with finite-valued A, let K be the total conditional channel from B to A. For every a,b, Pr(B = b) K(a | b) = Pr(A = a,B = b), including b of zero probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelJoint_cond: For a pair with finite-valued A, sampling B from its marginal and then A from the total conditional channel given B reproduces the joint law in the order (B,A).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_cha: Sample (A,B) from any joint law and draw C from a channel depending only on B. The resulting triple always satisfies A → B → C.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChainOf_c: For any function f and any pair of random variables X and Y under a common law, X → Y → f(Y) is a Markov chain.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_iff: When C has a finite alphabet, A → B → C is Markov exactly when its joint law can be obtained by sampling (A,B) from their marginal and then using the canonical channel from B to C. That channel uses the C marginal as its default at null values of B.

For finite-valued C, the joint law of (A,B,C) is Markov exactly when it equals the extension of the (A,B) marginal by the canonical conditional law of C given B, with the C marginal as default on null fibers.
If C is finite-valued, A → B → C is Markov exactly when there is a channel V from B to C such that p(a,b,c) = pᴬᴮ(a,b)V(c | b) for all a,b,c.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_markov: For a finite Markov triple A → B → C, I(A;B) = I(A;C) + I(A;B | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_mark: For finite-valued random variables X → Y → Z forming a Markov chain under the given source law, I(X;Y) = I(X;Z) + I(X;Y | Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_dataPr: For a finite joint law with A → B → C Markov, the endpoint mutual information satisfies I(A;C) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_data: For finite-valued random variables forming X → Y → Z under the source law, I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_dat: For finite-valued random variables forming a Markov chain X → Y → Z, H(X | Y) ≤ H(X | Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_dataP: If a finite joint law satisfies A → B → C, the conditional entropies satisfy H(A | B) ≤ H(A | C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_data: For finite-valued variables with X → Y → Z Markov, I(X;Z) = I(X;Y) exactly when X → Z → Y is also Markov.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_dataPr: For a finite Markov triple A → B → C, equality I(A;C) = I(A;B) holds if and only if A → C → B is Markov.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_dat: For finite-valued variables with X → Y → Z Markov, H(X | Y) = H(X | Z) if and only if X → Z → Y is also Markov.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_dataP: For a finite joint law with A → B → C Markov, equality H(A | B) = H(A | C) holds exactly when A → C → B is also Markov.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channe: Let A and B take values in finite alphabets. Given (A,B), draw C from a channel with a finite output alphabet whose row depends only on B. Then I(A;C) ≤ I(A;B).
Let A and B take values in finite alphabets. Given (A,B), draw C from a channel with a finite output alphabet whose row depends only on A. Then I(C;B) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_indepe: Suppose A, B, C and D have finite alphabets. Given (A,B), draw C and D independently, using a channel from A to C and a channel from B to D. Then I(C;D) ≤ I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channe: For finite alphabets, send X through channel W to Y and then through channel V to Z. For any input law, the cascade satisfies I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y).
For a cascade of two finite channels, the mutual information between the initial input and final output is at most the mutual information between that input and the first output, for every input law.
Send X through a channel with finite input and output alphabets, and call its output Y. For every deterministic map f from the output alphabet to a finite alphabet, I(X;f(Y)) ≤ I(X;Y).
